.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The potential for gales on Monday has been included in the HWO.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Mostly sunny, dry and above seasonable temps through Saturday.

2) Increasing potential for a coastal low pressure to affect the 
area with wind and rain Sunday into Monday. Minor coastal impacts 
possible due to approaching full moon on Tuesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Good agreement in deep layered ridging through Saturday, albeit
interrupted by a weak PAC shortwave moving thru the NE US
tonight/Fri AM. 

At the surface, strong surface high pressure will dominate the 
weather over much of the eastern half of the country through the end 
of the week and into the beginning of the weekend. A moderating 
airmass under ridging will have high temperatures running several 
degrees above normal (upper 50s to middle 60s) thru Saturday.

Given the clear and dry conditions under a weak pressure 
gradient, low temperatures tonight and Friday night, and 
potentially Saturday Night, will be largely determined by 
radiational cooling. Overall expect a gradual moderation in 
overnight lows to a few-several degrees above seasonable for 
late week into the weekend, particularly for urban and immediate
coastal areas.

With moderating Tds over the next few days increasing potential 
for radiational fog across outlying areas, particularly river 
valley areas. Patchy freezing fog possible in river valleys, and
sheltered interior areas and LI pine barrens tonight. This 
presents a low probability of black ice development on elevated 
surfaces (bridges, overpasses, etc.) with return flow allowing 
for a bit of low-level moisture.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
The latest modeling continues to indicate the potential for a
coastal storm to impact the area late Sun into Mon. It is likely
that the system will continue to present a forecast challenge,
with tropical and subtropical elements possible, along with
typical track and timing uncertainties. Refer to the NHC for 
any tropical/subtropical details.

The 00Z GFS and AI-GFS continue to suggest a wet scenario for
the area. The AI-GFS in particular is signaling a swath of 4 
inch rains from the Mid-Atlantic to Srn New England. Based on 
FFG of around 3 inches for 6 hours across the region, this could
translate into widespread minor flooding, with the potential 
for isold flash flooding in the most flood prone areas. The 00Z 
GEM supports the single low scenario of the GFS and AI-GFS, with
the 00Z ECMWF continuing to be somewhat of an outlier even when
compared to the ECMWF-AIFS.

Will continue to estimate the peak wind gusts with this sys in
the 30-40mph range based on a progged depth of the low in the
980s and a lack of strong high pres adjacent to the area. An
upward adjustment in the wind estimate will be needed if the low
drops deeper and maintains a track close to or inside the
benchmark.

Spring tides next week could support some minor tidal flooding 
impacts depending on the exact track and intensity of the low. 
ETSS guidance does not go out far enough yet, but the NYHOPS 
Ensemble does signal the potential for minor at the end of the 
fcst cycle Sun night.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
High pressure in control through the TAF period. 

VFR. 

Winds will be mainly light WSW to WNW to start this morning, 
then backing to the SW this afternoon, mainly under 10 kt. With
the exception of some high cirrus moving in late, clear skies 
prevail.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of SW wind shift could be an hour or two off. Winds may
even go more southerly with seabreeze enhancement.

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z Friday through Monday... 

Friday-Saturday: VFR.

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower conditions developing in RA.

Monday: MVFR or lower likely early in RA, improvement possible
PM. NW G20-25kt 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Winds and seas will remain below SCA lvls thru Sat with high
pres over the region. Low pres will produce building seas and 
increasing winds Sun into Mon. Seas on the ocean could build to 
5 ft or greater by the end of the day Sun, with gale force winds
possible on all waters Mon depending on the track and intensity
of the low.
